# 1 Enoch Chapter 65 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 65:4 — 'you have wrought great destruction on the earth' — the indictment formula

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Ye-have-wrought great-destruction-on-the-earth" | Archaic second person plural; literal |
| LOGOS | "You have wrought great destruction on the earth" | Modern; 'wrought' is formal but precise |
| PNEUMA | "You have brought terrible destruction on the earth" | 'Brought' for 'wrought'; 'terrible' for 'great' |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Wrought destruction' is a precise rendering of the Ge'ez idiom (making/doing destruction). PNEUMA's 'brought' is acceptable but loses the active sense of the Watchers' agency. 'Great' is the Ge'ez abi; PNEUMA's 'terrible' is interpretive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 65:7 — 'Azazel, you shall have no peace' — the verdict against the chief Watcher

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Azazel, thou-shalt-have-no-peace: a-severe-sentence-has-gone-forth-against-thee" | Archaic; preserves direct address |
| LOGOS | "Azazel, you shall have no peace; a severe sentence has gone forth against you" | Modern formal; preserves direct address |
| PNEUMA | "Azazel — you will have no peace. A severe verdict has been issued against you" | 'Verdict' for 'sentence'; more legal register |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'A severe sentence has gone forth against you' is the most accurate rendering of the Ge'ez forensic language. 'Sentence' (LOGOS) and 'verdict' (PNEUMA) are both good; 'sentence' is slightly more precise as it refers to the pronounced judgment.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 65:11 — 'length of days' — the Watchers' request for extended existence

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "forgiveness-and-length-[of days]" | Literal; bracketed addition |
| LOGOS | "forgiveness and length of days" | Preserves the idiom |
| PNEUMA | "forgiveness and extended life" | Interpretive; 'extended life' is the meaning |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Length of days' is the standard biblical idiom for long life (cf. Ps 21:4; Prov 3:16), and it should be preserved. PNEUMA's 'extended life' is accurate but loses the idiomatic quality.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
